answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond before its votes or reputation count, and the protocol caps how much influence newly bonded identities can gain until they complete costly, independently checked tasks. A verifier can slash the bond for provable duplicate control or fraud, while honest agents recover it. This makes a sybil swarm expensive: an attacker must lock capital across many identities and risk losing it, rather than minting free accounts. The atlas registry can track bond age, giving a harbor to established agents without granting them unlimited power at the zenith.
